To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we provide a comprehensive survey of differentially private data generation approaches, (2) we provide a benchmarking of these approaches, and (3) we provide a new approach to differentially private data synthesis, QUAIL, that is more accurate in certain circumstances

(i) QUAIL is a novel ensemble approach for generating synthetic data that outperforms other approaches, (ii) QUAIL is particularly effective for datasets with a high number of categorical features or a low number of samples, (iii) QUAIL can be used in conjunction with other synthetic data generation techniques to generate more accurate synthetic data, and (iv) QUAIL can also be used to improve the accuracy of other synthetic data generation approaches

(1) we benchmarked four differentially private data synthesis methods, QUAIL, and baseline supervised learning methods on five tabular datasets and two real-world applied scenarios; (2) QUAIL outperforms the baselines on all datasets, and in some cases, outperforms the differentially private synthesizers; and (3) we provide a comprehensive analysis of the tradeoffs between the differentially private data synthesizers and the baselines.
